title: Process
description: A business or operational process that delivers value. Classified by intent (operational/support/management) and audience (ECF domain whose work this most advances); stakeholders and actors are referenced from typed catalogs.

plain_language_name.description: Human-readable, business-familiar name (CR-MET-020). Must remain semantically equivalent to `name` - a familiar rendering, not an informal synonym. Mirrors the catalogue-side CR-BP-230 attribute set.

plain_language_description.description: Everyday explanation of what this entity represents in practical terms (CR-MET-020). Rendered in the catalogue README Part I. Must not restate the formal `description` verbatim (MECE); metamodel jargon denied by the catalogue HUM gates.

business_purpose.description: Why this entity exists and the business significance it carries (CR-MET-020).

practical_context.description: When and where the work is encountered in everyday operations (CR-MET-020).

agent_type.description: The kind of agent illustrated by the example: human (a person performs it), non-human (automation/system performs it), mixed (human-with-system) (CR-MET-020).

narrative.description: Office-relatable worked example of the entity being carried out by the stated agent type (CR-MET-020).

worked_example.description: Worked example of this entity being performed by an agent of type human or non-human (CR-MET-020). The nested `agent_type` enum is deliberately NOT registered as a top-level E005 classification: it is embedded, mirroring the catalogue attribute set.

external_references.description: CR-3P: identifiers in external systems. Never a substitute for the OpenDEA id (E004).

process_intent.description: The process's role in the enterprise. 'operational' executes defined recurring work; 'support' enables other processes without producing the primary output; 'management' decides, plans, allocates, or governs. See docs/process-type-taxonomy.md for boundary rules.

process_audience.description: The Enterprise Concept Framework (ECF) domain whose work this process most advances. Axiom-derived from the definition of 'enterprise' — see technehub-labs/dea-metaframework REPORT.md §2.
